PullRequest.Title: Show release video side-by-side
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Scenarios.Scenario: Open official release notes from an update, command, update menu, or post-update widget, with highlights video enabled or disabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: showContent awaits the release-note fetch, base resolution, Markdown rendering/code tokenization and sanitized HTML generation before setHtml; the existing webview shell then presents the document. Automatic-update opening is launched asynchronously and does not gate the rest of startup. The added layout runs once before HTML delivery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request the official Markdown document and consume it as text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per cold exact version, shared by concurrent requests; zero additional requests for a warm successful version. A failed attempt can be retried after cache removal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical URL construction, promise caching, failure eviction and request count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The note editor awaits the fetch; automatic-update startup does not await the opening.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse/sanitize Markdown HTML and serialize the document, scripts and telemetry manifest into webview HTML.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One rendering pipeline per opening. Official notes already passed through the same post-Markdown sanitization pipeline. The diff adds a small wrapper structure around the single accepted player and highlights list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Official openings already parsed, sanitized and serialized the complete document for media URL rewriting, tryouts and telemetry indexing; player markup used an initially open details element.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: HTML generation completes before setHtml; no new per-item serialization boundary is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deliver HTML over the existing MessagePort and construct/write the inner content frame.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One content message/frame update per committed opening; existing initialization queues messages until the webview is ready.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same message and frame count; fullscreen permission was false.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to display notes; the added fullscreen flag travels in the existing content message.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/workbench/contrib/update/browser/releaseNotesEditor.ts: renderBody CSP and rendered img/video/track elements
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser-load the existing external styles, document images, optional video poster and media resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Image operations follow authored resources and browser cache/coalescing. At most one accepted highlights player; preload remains none and autoplay/loop are excluded by the candidate sanitizer. Playback is not invoked on initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resources were rendered inside an initially open disclosure with preload none and no autoplay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing browser resource loading may affect presentation; video playback downloads are not newly required before reading notes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One release document per opening, its bytes/DOM nodes and code blocks; normally one highlights section and list. videoAvailable accepts at most one highlights-video candidate. Rendering visits the document, while added wrapper construction moves nodes in that highlights section once.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fetches coalesce per exact version; different versions may fetch independently. Existing request-generation checks discard superseded openings before/after rendering. Code highlighting remains asynchronous per code block with shared extension-registration/tokenization dependencies. Added DOM restructuring is synchronous and once per render, not per list item or frame.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing version-keyed promise cache joins concurrent official-note fetches and keeps successful results; failures delete the cache entry. Reopening still renders the document. Official openings already supply both mediaBaseUrl and telemetry, so the changed fast-return condition does not add sanitization passes to this workflow. Browser caching for stylesheet, images and poster remains unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: manager callers, cache ownership, render arguments, sanitization gate, bounded video acceptance and MessagePort/frame delivery were traced. No changed boundary fan-out or hot-path placement was established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings or representative release-document size measurements are available. Added section-level DOM work and browser layout have not been profiled.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is a bounded layout change on an existing per-opening rendering path; official openings do not acquire additional whole-document sanitizer passes or network/IPC calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use the developer action to open the active file as release notes, including a video-enabled preview without tryout links.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The active editor model is read in memory, Markdown and code blocks are rendered, then highlights are restructured and HTML delivered to the preview webview. The preview command awaits generation; there is no official-note fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Postprocess the already rendered document through safeSetInnerHtml, layoutReleaseHighlights and final sanitization/HTML serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional postprocessing pipeline only when preview previously qualified for the fast return and now has an enabled valid video. Cost scales with that preview document's HTML, not with playback or scroll events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Without mediaBaseUrl, telemetry or tryout links, returned the first sanitized Markdown result without this DOM postprocessing. Other previews already postprocessed it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before the explicitly requested preview is shown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve allowed local/remote resource containment and read requested preview image/media bytes through fileService.readFileStream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per actual local-resource request, including byte ranges. Warm non-range GETs can use existing service-worker ETag revalidation/304 responses rather than retransferring bytes; range responses read the requested span and are not cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same relative media paths, roots, containment checks and stream/range loading were available to the initially open video and preview images.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: May affect media/image availability, not Markdown model retrieval. Video data remains demand-loaded rather than autoplayed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deliver preview HTML and forward service-worker local-resource requests/responses using MessagePort and transferable streams.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One HTML message per committed preview; local-resource requests follow the browser's actual resources/ranges rather than list items. Existing Electron resource-response-body semaphore remains in place for service-worker-mediated loads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical content/resource transport and response-body concurrency control; only wrapper HTML and fullscreen flag differ.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: HTML delivery is required for presentation; resource responses independently unblock their consuming images/player.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active document and its DOM nodes/code blocks per explicit preview command. At most one accepted highlights player. No automatic per-keystroke preview refresh was found in the manager or command caller.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each explicit invocation renders once; existing show-request checks reject superseded results. New DOM postprocessing is sequential, once per render. Media files remain handled by existing browser/service-worker resource paths.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current-file previews deliberately bypass the official-note cache and have no telemetry/mediaBaseUrl. Before the diff, a preview without tryout links could return immediately after Markdown sanitization; now an enabled accepted video requires the existing postprocessing pipeline. Previews already requiring tryout rendering use that pipeline before and after.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added preview-only linear postprocessing and unchanged resource boundaries. No evidence establishes repeated refreshes, an unbounded input amplification, or media initialization caused by the new click initializer.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cost of extra preview-only document sanitization and prevalence of very large developer previews are unmeasured; no materially disruptive performance symptom is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence actionable performance bug. The additional one-time postprocessing implements the requested layout and remains off any per-input/per-frame path; no independently amplified resource-load mechanism was proven.

Scenarios.Scenario: Read/scroll/resize release notes and collect engagement samples with the side-by-side player.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Browser CSS grid/container layout determines highlights sizing. Existing navigation and telemetry sample scheduled frames read live geometry after presentation; their results do not gate reading or playback. Telemetry samples are handled by the host asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/workbench/contrib/update/browser/releaseNotesEditor.ts: highlights grid/container CSS and initializeReleaseNotesNavigation; src/vs/workbench/contrib/update/browser/releaseNotesTelemetry.ts: initializeReleaseNotesTelemetry/sample
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser style/layout and existing geometry reads for visible content, headings and the single player.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Responsive layout on browser invalidation; existing navigation uses binary search over headings. Each coalesced telemetry sample scans bounded regions and tryouts, then reads the one video's rectangles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Navigation and telemetry already used the same geometry reads and frame coalescing. Video checks were conditional on an initially open disclosure. CSS previously stacked the player rather than sizing it beside the list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the UI/frame path; no changed read-after-write loop or synchronous nested relayout was identified.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Post numeric engagement samples to the host and refresh host visibility tracking.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sample per scheduled presented frame, not per region or item. Existing activity messages are throttled to at most one per 250 ms. Removing disclosure toggle removes that scheduling source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same sample payload/cardinality and activity throttle, plus an existing toggle scheduling source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous observation; does not block the reading workflow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use the existing telemetry service to enqueue bounded engagement/video events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Video actions are deduplicated once per action per opening. Existing dwell snapshot/checkpoint logic governs content events; layout does not add one event per list item or frame.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same event reporting and deduplication; visible-video detection previously required disclosure.open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing asynchronous telemetry reporting is not a prerequisite to reading notes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Viewport events, document headings, highlights list items and existing tryout occurrences. Telemetry regions are capped at 512 and links at 4096. The changed video visibility check concerns one player and adds no collection-wide loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing requestAnimationFrame slots coalesce scroll/resize/ResizeObserver callbacks separately for navigation and telemetry to at most one pending frame each. No new JS resize observer or relayout loop is introduced. Video samples remain part of the existing sample message.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Navigation retains its existing section/target list, uses live positions and only updates aria-current when the selected link changes. Telemetry retains its existing bounded identity map and per-opening action deduplication. There is no new measurement cache or retained history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: actual frame coalescing, geometry reads, region bounds and telemetry deduplication were inspected. No diff-introduced synchronous layout feedback or boundary multiplicity was established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser layout costs at different viewport widths and scroll rates are unmeasured. Changed tests cover representative widths and list lengths structurally, not performance duration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Changed CSS and visibility semantics do not establish extra repeated JS work, IPC fan-out or a layout feedback loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start/pause highlights playback by clicking the player, use native controls/fullscreen, and close or replace the document.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new primary-surface click handler invokes native play or pause only after an explicit eligible click. Playback startup waits for normal media availability. Fullscreen is delegated through existing iframe permission plumbing. Closing/replacing content removes its browsing context and pagehide removes the new listener.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Native media playback downloads/decodes the existing source and any caption resources after the user requests playback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One player, with byte/range requests controlled by the native media stack and user playback/seeking. The diff adds an eligible surface-click trigger, not startup playback or per-highlight requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Native controls already allowed user-requested playback of the same source. The PR adds surface play/pause behavior while preserving no autoplay/preload none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Media availability determines playback startup; it does not delay note rendering or scrolling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Carry the fullscreen permission in existing frame creation/content messages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing permission/configuration update per webview/frame creation; zero additional IPC or frame instances solely for this flag.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same frame/content transport existed with fullscreen disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Permission enables user-requested fullscreen, without extra startup initialization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected video and eligible user clicks over that document's lifetime; at most one play/pause call per eligible event. There is no per-frame handler, preload increase, timer or accumulating player collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous click handler per video; play returns a native promise and is not awaited by the UI handler. No new batch of concurrent players/downloads is created. Native fullscreen uses the existing outer/inner frame rather than opening another webview.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing browser media/cache behavior is unchanged. Candidate sanitization still strips autoplay and loop and sets preload none. Telemetry video actions remain once-per-action-per-opening. New listener state is scoped to one document and disposed on pagehide.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: initialization only registers one handler, click filtering is explicit, play/pause is user-triggered, and pagehide removes both new listeners. No changed retained-resource lifecycle or eager media load is established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native network buffering/decode/fullscreen timings are browser-dependent and not measured; they do not change the demonstrated call cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Playback and fullscreen are intentionally user-triggered; the new document-scoped handler is bounded and cleaned up.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open release-notes accessibility help with the revised video-control description.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing accessible-view provider returns localized help text on request; only one text string changes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One help provider/content request, with a fixed set of strings independent of release-note size or video duration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing synchronous fixed-size text assembly; no changed queue, observer or asynchronous initialization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache changes or new retained state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the sole changed help line replaces localized text and adds no execution path or expensive boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No material performance uncertainty beyond negligible fixed-size text differences.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass over all six changed files and their complete diff pages against base c30f00e4c9f5c20d6f93f40f6bfe6925dda0c45f. Traced official/preview rendering, cached fetches, sanitizer and HTML transport, responsive geometry sampling, native playback/fullscreen, local-resource streaming and listener disposal. No high-confidence actionable diff-introduced performance findings or qualifying regression fixes were established. Static read-only review; measured browser/resource timings are unavailable.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
